subject: SprintBank throughput alarm — reserved-capacity shortfall / C-suite alert
messages:
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@sprintbank.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: SRE Team <sre@sprintbank.com>, Alex Li <alex.li@sprintbank.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency & 5xx spike on reserved pool — urgent

Tessa,

We're seeing a sustained latency increase and a sharp rise in 5xx errors against our reserved capacity (DBL-4532) starting ~08:45 PT this morning. P95 latency has gone from ~220ms to ~1.9s; token throughput is falling and many requests are queueing. Our users are experiencing failures in checkout flows.

Attached: sprintbank_qps_graph.png (hourly qps + error rate), error_samples (few request/response traces).

We are on a reserved Dedicated pool, no config changes on our side. Can you confirm this is not a client-side regression and urgently advise next steps? We need mitigation within the hour — this is impacting revenue.

Morgan Lee
SRE Lead, SprintBank

---

(Attachment: sprintbank_error_samples.zip)

Morgan — thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments. We're looking immediately.

Short answers up front:
- We're opening an internal incident and will route it to Dedicated runtime ops and the SRE-on-call.
- Please keep sending traces and example request IDs; that helps root cause faster.
- I'll coordinate a temporary mitigation (burst authorization + model fallback) while we diagnose.

Naomi (CS lead) and Karthik (SRE liaison) are looped for operational actions and escalation. I will provide status updates every 30 minutes until we stabilize.

Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden latency & 5xx spike on reserved pool — urgent

Team — quick ops proposal based on initial telemetry (I reviewed the attachments):

Observations:
- Error patterns indicate overload-induced 5xx (OOM/timeout) rather than model-level hallucination.
- QPS increased ~2.4x during a traffic burst window; our Dedicated pool for SprintBank appears saturated and auto-burst did not trigger — possible burst auth boundary.

Immediate mitigations (30–90m):
1) Authorize a short-term burst to the next capacity tier (ops). This buys headroom (~45–75m) for an engineered rollback.
2) Apply request-rate smoothing in the gateway (per-customer token throttling, gentle 429 to upstream with Retry-After) — reduces queue depth.
3) Enable fallback to a slightly smaller model variant for non-critical routes (cost: tiny quality delta).
4) Engage runtime team to inspect kernel-level latency (KV cache pressure).

I recommend we escalate to CRO and Head of Runtime to approve immediate burst and credit remediation. We should also issue a brief to SprintBank with a mutual action plan (MAP). I've drafted a MAP — attached as 2026-10-29-sprintbank_map.docx.

I'll stand by to convert this into an exec note if Tessa wants to send up.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: 2026-10-29-sprintbank_map.docx)

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@sprintbank.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: URGENT: SprintBank reserved-capacity shortfall — request for exec authorization

Karthik / Jordan — we need immediate exec authorization for a short burst and to approve credits/SLR for SprintBank (DBL-4532). Customer impact: live checkout failures, elevated 5xx and P95 latency ~2s.

Summary of current state:
- Root cause hypothesis: Dedicated pool saturation during an unexpected traffic spike; KV cache pressure increased latency and caused timeouts.
- Mitigations in motion: Naomi initiated gateway smoothing; Ops ready to trigger burst with your approval; we can flip non-critical routes to fallback model to reduce load.
- Customer ask: mitigation within 30–60 minutes and a timeline for permanent remediation (permanent capacity increase or revised autoscaling policy).

Requested approvals:
1) Authorize a one-hour burst to the next capacity tier.
2) Approve a goodwill credit and a joint post-incident review (SprintBank prefers a commercial gesture).
3) Loop CTO/runtime (optionally) if kernel patch is required.

Naomi has attached a proposed MAP and timeline. I'll be on the call with SprintBank SRE at 16:40 PT to coordinate. Please reply with authorization or a short note if you want Ops to proceed without a full exec huddle.

Thanks — we need a quick yes/no.

Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
